name: java-vsix-lite
description: Minimal, low-compute Java language support for VS Code (pure-Rust default tier; optional opt-in javac tier).

virtualWorkspaces.description: This extension launches a native language-server process and reads project files from a physical filesystem, so it does not run in virtual (non-filesystem) workspaces.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The pure-Rust default tier (highlighting, structure, lint, signature IntelliSense) runs in untrusted workspaces — it never executes project code and never touches the network. The optional javac tier, the consent-gated dependency download, Install Dependencies (which runs the project's Maven/Gradle build scripts), and debugging (which launches project code in a JVM) all stay disabled until the workspace is trusted.

java-vsix-lite.server.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `jvl-server` binary. Leave empty to use the bundled binary. The `JVL_SERVER_PATH` environment variable overrides this. **Machine-scoped on purpose**: a workspace must never be able to redirect which binary is launched as the language server.

java-vsix-lite.trace.server.description: Trace the JSON-RPC traffic between VS Code and the language server (for debugging).

java-vsix-lite.diagnostics.unresolvedMem.markdownDescription: Report an error for a member access (`obj.foo()`) when the receiver's type **and its entire supertype chain** resolve but declare no such member. Conservative: stays silent whenever resolution is incomplete (an unknown supertype, a missing dependency JAR, generics). On by default; disable if you hit a false positive on a hierarchy the resolver can't fully see.

java-vsix-lite.diagnostics.unused.markdownDescription: Report a warning (with the *unnecessary code* fade) for unused local variables, unused parameters of constructors and `private`/`static` methods, and unreferenced `private` fields and methods. Detection is name-occurrence based within the file, so shadowing can only cause silence, never a false warning; `@Override` methods, `main`, catch/lambda parameters, annotated members, and `serialVersionUID` are always skipped. On by default; disable to hide the warnings.

java-vsix-lite.jdk.home.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a JDK home to use for `Check Project (javac)`, tried before `$JAVA_HOME`. Leave empty to use `$JAVA_HOME`. Never downloaded — if neither resolves to a real `javac`, the check fails with a clear error. **Machine-scoped on purpose**: a workspace must never be able to point `javac` at a binary it ships.

java-vsix-lite.javac.timeoutSecs.markdownDescription: How long `Check Project (javac)` waits before killing `javac`, in seconds. Clamped to 10–600.

java-vsix-lite.javac.checkOnSave.markdownDescription: Run a background `javac` check automatically when the project loads and after saving a Java file, publishing real compiler errors to Problems. These automatic checks are **module-scoped**: only the Maven/Gradle module(s) owning the saved file(s) are compiled (sibling-module sources are still resolved, via `-sourcepath`), so unrelated modules aren't recompiled on every save. The manual **Java: Check Project (javac)** command remains a full-workspace check. Debounced, one run at a time, and silent (no pop-ups — results land in Problems only). Only active in a **trusted** workspace, because it spawns the JDK's `javac`; in an untrusted workspace saves never trigger it. Uses the same JDK resolution and timeout as the manual command.

java-vsix-lite.dependencies.repository.markdownDescription: Base URL of the Maven repository to download missing dependencies from, e.g. an internal Artifactory/Nexus proxy in a governed network: `https://artifacts.example.com/maven2`. Empty means Maven Central. Must be a plain `https://` URL — no credentials, query, or fragment; anything else disables downloads rather than silently falling back. **Machine-scoped on purpose**: a workspace (repository) must never be able to redirect where your dependency downloads come from. Checksum sidecar verification applies to any repository, unchanged.

java-vsix-lite.maven.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `mvn` executable used by `Install Dependencies (runs build tool)`. Leave empty to use the project's `mvnw` wrapper if present, otherwise `mvn` on `PATH`. **Machine-scoped on purpose**: a workspace must never be able to choose which executable is run on your behalf.

java-vsix-lite.gradle.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `gradle` executable used by `Install Dependencies (runs build tool)`. Leave empty to use the project's `gradlew` wrapper if present, otherwise `gradle` on `PATH`. **Machine-scoped on purpose**: a workspace must never be able to choose which executable is run on your behalf.

java-vsix-lite.dependencies.autoDownload.markdownDescription: What to do when missing dependencies are detected, in a trusted workspace: `prompt` asks once per session with a Download / Always / Never choice; `always` downloads silently from then on (same HTTPS + checksum verification, Maven Central only, as `Java: Download Missing Dependencies`); `never` disables the automatic check (the manual command still works). Choosing Always or Never from the prompt updates this setting for the current workspace.

mainClass.description: Fully-qualified name of the class whose main method to run, e.g. com.example.Main.

args.description: Program arguments passed to the main method.

vmArgs.description: JVM arguments (each a separate argv element, never shell-parsed).

cwd.description: Working directory of the program. Defaults to projectRoot.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the program (overlaid on the inherited environment).

projectRoot.description: Project folder used to derive the classpath and source roots. Defaults to the workspace folder.

classPaths.description: Explicit classpath entries. When set, they are used exactly as given; when empty, existing Maven/Gradle build output plus resolved dependency jars are used, falling back to a one-shot javac -g compile.

stopOnEntry.description: Break on the first line of the main method.

hostName.description: Host of the JVM to attach to (started with -agentlib:jdwp=transport=dt_socket,server=y).

port.description: JDWP port of the JVM to attach to.

timeout.description: How long to retry the connection, in milliseconds.

projectRoot.description: Project folder used to discover source roots for stack traces. Defaults to the workspace folder.

sourcePaths.description: Extra source root directories probed when resolving stack-frame sources.
